planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Ant Admire is a Chinese-origin selection valued for large, elongated, dark chocolate-brown fruit that holds its crisp texture longer after picking than most varieties.

directions: Ant Admire is a Chinese-origin jujube selection valued for its large, elongated, chocolate-brown fruit that ripens early to midseason and holds its crisp texture unusually well after harvest, extending the window for fresh out-of-hand eating. Trees are grown like other jujube cultivars, needing full sun and tolerating poor, dry soils once established. The fruit's sweetness and firm hold after picking make it useful for both fresh snacking and for growers who want a longer harvest window without quick textural decline.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Black Sea is noted for cropping reliably even as a young tree and for tolerating wetter, more humid conditions better than many jujube selections.

directions: Black Sea, also sold as 'Russian 2', traces to Ukraine and was imported to US collections by jujube grower James Gilbert. It produces small, ovoid, dark brown-red fruit that ripens early and sets a strong crop even on young trees, and it handles wetter, more humid growing conditions better than many other jujube selections, a useful trait for Gulf Coast gardens with heavy summer rainfall. Like other jujube cultivars it should be planted in full sun on well-drained soil and needs little irrigation once established. Its early productivity on young wood makes it a good choice for gardeners who want fruit sooner rather than waiting many years for a mature tree.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Ed Hegard is a thornless, mid-season Alabama selection whose fruit closely resembles the widely grown Lang and Thornless cultivars.

directions: Ed Hegard is a thornless jujube selection that originated in Alabama, with fruit character very similar to the widely grown Lang and Thornless cultivars. It bears on roughly the same mid-season schedule as those other selections, so it makes a reasonable companion planting where Lang is already grown. As with other jujube types, full sun and minimal supplemental water are sufficient once the tree is established, and the absence of spines makes harvest and pruning easier.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; GI-1183 is a late-season selection from the historic USDA Chico, California breeding program, producing large, sweet fruit.

directions: GI-1183 is one of the historic USDA Chico, California breeding program selections, part of the same program that also released Chico, GA-866, and Thornless. It ripens late in the jujube season and produces large, sweet fruit. It shares the vigorous, drought-tolerant growth habit typical of jujube and performs reliably across a range of soils as long as drainage is adequate. GI-1183 is a good option for growers wanting a Chico-program selection to extend the harvest season beyond earlier-ripening cultivars.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Globe is a Chinese variety from Henan Province, imported to US collections in the 1990s, producing round fruit prized mainly for drying.

directions: Globe is a jujube variety from Henan Province, China, imported into US collections in the 1990s and grown for its notably round fruit, which is prized primarily for drying rather than fresh eating since the fresh fruit is comparatively mild and plain in flavor. Dried, the fruit develops good sweetness and chewiness, making Globe a useful variety for growers focused on dried jujube production rather than fresh snacking. It grows and fruits on the same general timeline as other jujube cultivars and tolerates the same range of heat, drought, and soil conditions.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Jin produces uniform, elongated, small-seeded fruit that dries to an intensely chewy texture.

directions: Jin produces uniform, elongated fruit with an unusually small seed relative to its size. It is particularly well suited to drying, where the fruit develops an intensely chewy, date-like texture once left to dry on the tree. Growers who want a jujube cultivar optimized for the dried 'Chinese date' use rather than fresh eating should consider Jin alongside other drying-type selections.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; La Fleur is a vigorously growing selection with small, notably juicy fruit.

directions: La Fleur is a vigorously growing jujube cultivar that produces small fruit with a notably juicy texture compared to many larger-fruited selections. The vigorous habit means it establishes and fills its allotted space quickly, which can be an advantage for growers wanting faster canopy development. Fruit quality leans toward fresh eating, where the juiciness is most appreciated before the fruit begins to dry and wrinkle on the tree.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Norris #1 was identified from historic TVA plantings near Norris Dam, Tennessee and introduced by Hidden Springs Nursery of Cookeville, TN.

directions: Norris #1 was identified from historic Tennessee Valley Authority plantings near Norris Dam in eastern Tennessee and has proven to be an abundant, dependable jujube selection in humid eastern climates. Its origin in a wetter, more humid growing region makes it a reasonable option for Gulf Coast gardeners concerned about jujube performance outside the arid West where the genus is more typically grown. Plant and manage it like other jujube cultivars, in full sun with good drainage and minimal supplemental watering once established.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Thornless is a bud-mutation selection of 'Lang' found at the USDA Chico Plant Introduction Station, grown with few or no spines, easing harvest and maintenance.

directions: Thornless is a spineless bud mutation of the popular 'Lang' cultivar, selected at the USDA Chico Plant Introduction Station by researchers Ackerman and Smith, and true to its name grows with few or no spines, making harvest and tree maintenance noticeably easier than with most jujube cultivars. The oval to pear-shaped fruit turns a reddish-brown at full ripeness and is grown mainly as a drying type, with fruit character very close to Lang. Its fruit character is close to Lang, so it fills a similar niche while offering the practical benefit of a nearly spine-free tree.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Topeka is a very late-cropping selection that originated in eastern Kansas.

directions: Topeka is a late-cropping jujube selection that originated in eastern Kansas, illustrating the species' tolerance for a wider range of North American climates than its desert-Southwest reputation might suggest. Its very late ripening window extends the jujube harvest season when grown alongside earlier selections such as Li or Honey Jar. As with other jujubes, it performs best in full sun on well-drained soil and needs very little irrigation once established.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Xu Zhou is a Chinese selection that begins bearing at a young tree age and ripens its elongated fruit late in the season.

directions: Xu Zhou is a Chinese jujube selection that begins bearing fruit at an unusually young tree age compared to many other cultivars, and it also tolerates wetter growing conditions reasonably well. The elongated fruit ripens late in the season, extending the harvest window when grown alongside earlier-ripening cultivars. Otherwise it is managed like any other jujube, needing full sun and tolerating a wide range of soils once established.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Yazoo Li was found naturalized in Yazoo City, Mississippi by Taylor Yowell and is believed to be a seedling of the classic Li cultivar.

directions: Yazoo Li is a jujube selection found naturalized in Yazoo City, Mississippi by grower Taylor Yowell, believed to have originated as a seedling of the classic Li cultivar, and sources vary on whether its fruit runs larger than Li or about the same size, though both describe good sweetness. The vigorous, upright tree ripens its crop early, typically in late August in the Deep South, ahead of many other large-fruited selections. Its Mississippi origin and documented performance in the humid Southeast make it a particularly good match for Gulf Coast growing conditions.
